# Command line: vcc

vcc is the command-line tool of VintageCoder. It translates assembler and BASIC for C64, C128, Plus/4, VIC-20, Atari 8-bit and MEGA65, creates projects, builds disks and runs tests.

Help in the program: `vcc --help`, `vcc help <command>`, `vcc <command> --help`. Manual pages: `vcc man <command>`; completion: `vcc completion <shell>`.

**Build programs:** [`asm`](#vcc-asm), [`basic`](#vcc-basic), [`basic2asm`](#vcc-basic2asm), [`build`](#vcc-build)

**Projects:** [`add`](#vcc-add), [`migrate`](#vcc-migrate), [`new`](#vcc-new), [`organize`](#vcc-organize), [`turbo`](#vcc-turbo)

**Media and data:** [`dis`](#vcc-dis), [`disk`](#vcc-disk), [`import`](#vcc-import), [`inc`](#vcc-inc), [`media`](#vcc-media), [`roms`](#vcc-roms)

**Test and measure:** [`emulator`](#vcc-emulator), [`streams`](#vcc-streams), [`test`](#vcc-test)

**Help and feedback:** [`debuglog`](#vcc-debuglog), [`feedback`](#vcc-feedback), [`update`](#vcc-update)

## `vcc add`

Add files and folders to the project

Adds files the same way as dropping them in the IDE: detects the kind, picks the category and target folder from rules and layout in the project file, copies the file and enters it in assets. If the source is already in the project folder, it stays there and is only entered.

Folders are added recursively and keep their subfolders. Hidden files, target and node_modules are left out. At most 5000 files per folder.

```
vcc add <file|folder>... [options]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file|folder` | Files or folders to add. Can be repeated. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--into` `<project>` | Project folder or .vcprj file. | `.` |
| `--dir` `<folder>` | Target folder in the project (relative, without ..). Overrides the folder of the category. For folders, the subfolder structure is appended. | folder of the category from layout |
| `--flat` | Put files from folders without subfolders, each in the folder of its category (or --dir). |  |
| `--category` `<category>` | Category for all files (source, text/docs, binary data, raw graphics data, raw character set). Values: `source`, `text`, `binary`, `graphics`, `charset`. | detected from rules, file name and content |
| `--description` `<text>` | Description that is also entered in assets. |  |
| `--conflict` `<rule>` | What to do if another file with this name is already at the target: save under a new name (name_2), replace or skip. Values: `rename`, `replace`, `skip`. | `rename` |
| `--dry-run` | Only show what would happen (target state, target, kind, category). Copies nothing, project file unchanged. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Add a file
vcc add sprites.bin --into game
```

```bash
# Add a folder with its structure
vcc add images --category graphics --into game
```

```bash
# Add a folder flat into one target folder
vcc add music --flat --dir data/music --description "Title music"
```

```bash
# preview only
vcc add images --into game --dry-run
```

> **Note:** If the project folder has no .vcprj, the command stops. Errors with single files give exit code 1; the other files are still added.

> **Note:** Disk images, PRG and XEX files are taken by vcc import.

## `vcc asm`

Assemble assembler source

Assembles a single assembler file and writes the result in the chosen output format. The target system comes from --target (default c64). Without --cpu, the CPU of the target is used.

If the source contains .cartridge and --format is missing, the output is a cartridge (crt for the C64, car for the Atari, vic20cart for the VIC-20). Otherwise it is the default format of the target. Without -o, the output has the name of the source with the extension of the format. To build a whole project, use vcc build.

```
vcc asm <file.asm> [options]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file.asm` | Assembler source. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-o` `<file>` | Output file. | source name with the extension of the format |
| `--target` `<system>` | Target system: sets the CPU, chip symbols, text code and default format. Values: `atari8`, `c128`, `c64`, `mega65`, `pet`, `plus4`, `vic20`. | `c64` |
| `--cpu` `<cpu>` | CPU instruction set, if it differs from the target. Values: `45gs02`, `6510`, `7501`, `8502`, `nmos6502`, `sally`. | CPU of the target system |
| `--format` `<format>` | Output format. d64, d71 and d81 put the program as the only file in a new disk image. a0, 20, 40 and 60 create a VIC-20 cartridge for the given memory block. Values: `prg`, `bin`, `xex`, `crt`, `car`, `rom`, `d64`, `d71`, `d81`, `vic20cart`, `a0`, `20`, `40`, `60`. | default format of the target system; a cartridge if the source has .cartridge |
| `--memory` `<expansion>` | Memory expansion of the VIC-20. Sets the BASIC start, screen memory and color memory. No effect on other targets. Values: `unexpanded`, `3k`, `8k`, `16k`, `24k`, `35k`. | unexpanded (VIC-20 only) |
| `--cart` `<type>` | Cartridge type for crt, car and rom. Replaces the .cartridge setting in the source. Values: `normal`, `8k`, `16k`, `ocean`, `magicdesk`, `easyflash`, `actionreplay`, `ar`, `ultimax`, `xegs`. | C64: normal; Atari: derived from the code |
| `--illegals` `<regel>` | How to handle undocumented instructions: deny reports an error, warn a warning, allow nothing. Values: `deny`, `warn`, `allow`. | `warn` |
| `-I` `<ordner>` | Extra search folder for include files. data/sys is always searched last. Can be repeated. |  |
| `-D` `<name[=number]>` | Defines a constant for .if and .ifdef. Without =number the value is 1. Write numbers as 42, $2a, 0x2a or %101010. Can be repeated. |  |
| `--labels` `<datei.vs>` | Writes the labels as a VICE label file. |  |
| `--debug` `<datei.vcdbg>` | Writes the debug information (for the debugger and tests). |  |
| `--listing` `<datei.lst>` | Writes the listing with addresses and bytes. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<ordner>` | Folder of the hardware database (data). Replaces VC_DATA and the automatic search. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# assemble (target C64)
vcc asm examples/c64/border/border.asm -o border.prg
```

```bash
# MEGA65 program with a test constant
vcc asm examples/mega65/prallball/prallball.asm -o prallball.prg --target mega65 --cpu 45gs02 --illegals deny -D START_HIRES=1
```

```bash
# Atari program as XEX
vcc asm examples/atari/colorbars/colorbars.asm -o colorbars.xex --target atari8 --format xex
```

```bash
# C64 cartridge with several banks
vcc asm examples/c64/cart_demo/cart_demo.asm -o cart_oc.crt --format crt --cart ocean -D OCEAN=1 --labels cart_oc.vs
```

> **Note:** Any other value for --format creates a PRG file with that extension. --cart and --cpu are only checked during assembly and then report an error.

> **Note:** For cartridges, the assembler fills unused areas with $FF. The banks come from .bank and .org in the source.

> **Note:** A VIC-20 cartridge at $A000 needs the signature A0CBM at $A004 in the source.

Exit codes: `0` = assembled (warnings possible) · `1` = error in the source, while writing or in an option value · `2` = wrong usage

## `vcc basic`

Tokenize BASIC, read it back, print the syntax tree

Without further options, vcc basic translates a native BASIC program (line numbers optional, jump labels @name) into the storage format of the target system: PRG on Commodore, SAVE format (.bas) on Atari. The forms --tokenize and --detokenize work on the token level only. vcc basic ast prints the syntax tree.

The files are in the data folder. vcc finds it through --data-dir, VC_DATA, the location of the program or the working folder.

### Basic form

translate native BASIC to PRG (Commodore) or BAS (Atari)

```
vcc basic <file.bas|file.lst|file.tur> [optionen]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file` | Source text. The extensions .bas, .lst and .tur (or --plain) select native BASIC. .sbas is switched off. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--target` `<system>` | Target system (file in data/targets), e.g. c64, c128, plus4, mega65, vic20, pet or atari8. | `c64` |
| `--dialect` `<id>` | BASIC dialect (file in data/basic): cbm_v2, basic7, basic35, basic65, atari_basic or turbo_basic_xl. | dialect of the target system |
| `--memory` `<memory>` | Memory expansion of the target. It sets the BASIC start address. Only the VIC-20 has it (unexpanded, 3k, 8k, 16k, 24k, 35k). Other targets ignore it. | default of the target (VIC-20: unexpanded) |
| `--plain` | Read the source text as native BASIC, even with an extension other than .bas, .lst and .tur. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder with the hardware database (data). | VC_DATA or next to the program |
| `-o` `<output>` | Output file. For native BASIC it must not be the source file. | source name with .prg (Commodore) or .bas (Atari) |
| `--start` `<n>` | Number of the first line without its own line number. An invalid number is silently replaced by the default. A line #numbering start=N step=N in the file takes precedence; step at least 1, on overflow B192 suggests a smaller one. | `10` |
| `--step` `<n>` | Step size of the automatic line numbers. An invalid number is silently replaced by the default. A line #numbering start=N step=N in the file takes precedence; step at least 1, on overflow B192 suggests a smaller one. | `10` |
| `--check` | Check only: print warnings (B150–B159, B167), write no file. |  |
| `--compact` | Remove spaces inside statements where that changes nothing (Commodore only; saves memory and run time). Strings, REM and DATA stay. |  |
| `--no-check` | Skip the syntax check while translating. |  |
| `--disable` `<codes>` | Switch off individual warnings, codes separated by commas (e.g. B150,B154). Errors cannot be switched off. |  |
| `-I` `<folder>` | Search folder for included files. The first one is also the root for machine code includes. Can be repeated. | working folder (root) |
| `-D` `<NAME=number>` | Set a constant for the source text (native BASIC: acts like #define NAME number). Can be repeated. |  |
| `--pack` | Combine lines (Commodore only). |  |
| `--map` `<file>` | Write the mapping of source name to BASIC name and label to line into a text file (Commodore only). |  |
| `--labels` `<file>` | Read a VICE label file. Its addresses are available in the source text as constants asm.name (Commodore only). |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Translate a C64 program with jump labels
vcc basic examples/c64/basic_native/sterne.bas -o sterne.prg
```

```bash
# Translate an Atari BASIC program
vcc basic examples/atari/basic_native/farben.bas --target atari8 -o farben.bas
```

```bash
# Translate Turbo BASIC XL
vcc basic examples/atari/turbo_basic/balken.tur --target atari8 --dialect turbo_basic_xl -o balken.bas
```

```bash
# VIC-20 with 8 KB expansion
vcc basic examples/c64/basic_native/sterne.bas --target vic20 --memory 8k -o sterne.prg
```

> **Note:** #include brings in files and media (e.g. #include "graphics/hero.vcsprite" as DATA; project folder = nearest folder with a project file); media are read during conversion (--to-labels, --to-numbers, --renumber) but never written back.

> **Note:** Directives in native BASIC: #define NAME value (replacement before numbering), #if SYSTEM_C64 / #else / #endif, #dialect <id> (dialect of this file) and #asm "file.asm" [with "song.asm"] (machine code behind the BASIC text or as DATA lines; the symbols appear in the program as asm.name).

> **Note:** The output lists the labels (@name = line n) and, with #longnames, the mapping of the long names. A .sbas file is rejected.

> **Note:** The options -I, --pack, --map and --labels only work when translating source text with an extension other than .bas, .lst and .tur without --plain. For native BASIC they are accepted but not used. The option -D also works for native BASIC (like a #define).

### Form `tokenize`

tokenize a classic numbered listing

```
vcc basic --tokenize <list.lst> [optionen]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `list` | Listing with a line number on every line, without labels and without directives. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--tokenize` | Switches to this form. Required. |  |
| `--target` `<system>` | Target system (file in data/targets). It sets the dialect and the load address. | `c64` |
| `--dialect` `<id>` | BASIC dialect (file in data/basic). | dialect of the target system |
| `--memory` `<memory>` | Memory expansion of the target. It sets the load address (VIC-20: unexpanded, 3k, 8k, 16k, 24k, 35k). | default of the target |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder with the hardware database (data). | VC_DATA or next to the program |
| `-o` `<output>` | Output file. | source name with .prg (Commodore) or .bas (Atari) |

Examples:

```bash
# Tokenize a listing to PRG
vcc basic --tokenize liste.lst --target c64 -o liste.prg
```

> **Note:** A line without a line number is an error (B100). For source text with labels and directives, use the form without --tokenize.

### Form `detokenize`

print a PRG or Atari SAVE file as a listing

```
vcc basic --detokenize <file.prg> [optionen]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `datei` | Commodore PRG or Atari BASIC file in SAVE format. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--detokenize` | Switches to this form. Required. |  |
| `--target` `<system>` | Target system (file in data/targets). For Atari files, give atari8. Without it, the Commodore PRG format applies. | `c64` |
| `--dialect` `<id>` | BASIC dialect (file in data/basic). It provides the word list to translate the tokens back. | dialect of the target system |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder with the hardware database (data). | VC_DATA or next to the program |
| `--structured` | Print text with labels (@L10) instead of the classic listing. Commodore only. |  |
| `-o` `<output>` | Write the listing to a file. | output to stdout |

Examples:

```bash
# Read a PRG as a listing
vcc basic --detokenize stars.prg
```

```bash
# Convert an Atari file back to a text file
vcc basic --detokenize colors.bas --target atari8 -o colors.lst
```

> **Note:** Keywords appear in lower case on Commodore and in upper case on Atari. Control characters appear as {clr} and so on. If the file starts with two zero bytes, the error message points to --target atari8.

### Form `suggest-hex`

show hex suggestions for chip register addresses or apply selected ones

```
vcc basic --suggest-hex <datei.bas|datei.lst> [optionen]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `datei` | Native BASIC with decimal addresses (e.g. an imported program). |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--suggest-hex` | Switches to this form. Required. |  |
| `--target` `<system>` | Target system (file in data/targets). It sets the dialect and the known chip registers. | `c64` |
| `--dialect` `<id>` | BASIC dialect (file in data/basic). | dialect of the target system |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder with the hardware database (data). | VC_DATA or next to the program |
| `--apply` `<list>` | Numbers of the suggestions (from the list, separated by commas) to write to the output file. Without --apply, the suggestions are only listed. Nothing is ever changed without a selection. | list only |
| `-o` `<output>` | Output file for --apply (the source file is never overwritten). |  |

Examples:

```bash
# View the suggestions
vcc basic --suggest-hex game.bas --target c64
```

```bash
# Apply suggestions 1 and 3
vcc basic --suggest-hex game.bas --apply 1,3 -o game_hex.bas
```

> **Note:** Only complete decimal addresses from 256 upward are suggested, as an argument of POKE, PEEK, SYS, WAIT and USR, and only if they are a chip register of the target system. Arithmetic expressions, DATA and strings are left untouched.

### Form `convert`

Convert line numbers to labels, labels to line numbers, or renumber

```
vcc basic (--to-labels | --to-numbers | --renumber) <datei.bas|datei.lst|datei.tur> [optionen]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `datei.bas` | BASIC source; included files (#include) are converted along with it. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--to-labels` | Convert line numbers to labels: only lines that are jumped to get a label, existing names are kept. Computed jump targets (GOTO A*10) abort the conversion (B162). |  |
| `--to-numbers` | Convert labels to line numbers: always renumbered; the names are kept as marker lines ;@name. |  |
| `--renumber` | Renumber the lines and adjust all jump targets. |  |
| `--range` `<a-b>` | Renumber only lines whose old number is from a to b (with --renumber, line-number mode only). |  |
| `--start` `<n>` | First line number. A line #numbering start=N step=N in the file takes precedence; step at least 1, on overflow B192 suggests a smaller one. | `10` |
| `--step` `<n>` | Line number step. A line #numbering start=N step=N in the file takes precedence; step at least 1, on overflow B192 suggests a smaller one. | `10` |
| `-o` `<datei>` | Write the result (main file only) to this file. | standard output |
| `--write` | Overwrite all changed files in place. |  |
| `--preview` | Only list the changed lines (old → new), write nothing. |  |
| `--target` `<system>` | Target system (file in data/targets); determines the dialect. | `c64` |
| `--dialect` `<id>` | BASIC dialect (file in data/basic); a line #dialect <id> in the file takes precedence. | dialect of the target system |
| `--data-dir` `<ordner>` | Folder with the hardware database (data). | VC_DATA or next to the program |

Examples:

```bash
# Preview of the conversion to labels
vcc basic --to-labels spiel.bas --preview
```

```bash
# Convert to line numbers and overwrite the file
vcc basic --to-numbers spiel.bas --write
```

```bash
# Renumber from 100 in steps of 5
vcc basic --renumber spiel.bas --start 100 --step 5 -o neu.bas
```

> **Note:** The mode of a file follows from its content; a mix of numbers and labels (B160) can be resolved with either conversion.

> **Note:** The names of manually assigned labels are kept as a line ;@name before the statement and reused when converting back.

Exit codes: `0` = Conversion succeeded · `1` = Conversion not possible (error B1xx)

### Form `ast`

print the syntax tree of a BASIC program

```
vcc basic ast <file.bas> [optionen]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file.bas` | BASIC source text (the same reader as in basic2asm). |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--target` `<system>` | Target system. It sets the BASIC dialect. Values: `c64`, `c128`, `plus4`, `mega65`, `atari8`. | `c64` |
| `--turbo` | Read the source text as Turbo BASIC XL (target atari8 only). |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder with the hardware database (data). | VC_DATA or next to the program |
| `--json` | Print the tree as JSON (lines, statements, expressions; strings as byte lists). | Rust debug output of the lines |
| `--roundtrip` | Print the tree as canonical text, read it back and report E191 if the tree is not the same. Takes precedence over --json. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Syntax tree as JSON
vcc basic ast examples/c64/basic_native/sterne.bas --json
```

```bash
# Check the round trip
vcc basic ast examples/c64/basic_native/sterne.bas --roundtrip
```

> **Note:** The call uses the parser of basic2asm. Its other options (-o, --map, --stage, --float, --int-div, --style, --runtime, --no-track-line, --no-rem, --check) are accepted but have no effect here.

> **Note:** Statements that the converter does not translate (OPEN, LOAD ...) cannot be written back (E190).

Exit codes: `0` = tree printed, or round trip OK · `1` = error in the source text, or round trip not OK

## `vcc basic2asm`

Convert a BASIC program to assembler source

Converts a BASIC program to readable assembler source that runs as a machine program. Each BASIC line becomes a section with the original as a comment and the label L<line>. Besides the .asm file, a line map (JSON) is created for the debugger.

The converter picks the smallest stage the program needs: 1 = integer, 2 = floating point, 3 = strings. --stage sets the upper limit.

```
vcc basic2asm <file.bas> [options]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file.bas` | BASIC source. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--target` `<system>` | Target system. Sets the start address, processor and BASIC dialect. The MEGA65 has no floating point (E331). Values: `c64`, `c128`, `plus4`, `mega65`, `atari8`. | `c64` |
| `--turbo` | Read the source as Turbo BASIC XL (target atari8 only, otherwise E344). Blocks like WHILE/WEND and PROC/EXEC become jumps. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder with the hardware database (data). With --runtime embed, also the source of the runtime. | VC_DATA or next to the program |
| `--stage` `<1\|2\|3>` | Highest allowed stage. The smallest one the program needs is chosen. Numbers other than 1 to 3 report E300. | `3` |
| `--float` | Include the floating-point runtime even if the program does not need it. |  |
| `--int-div` | Translate / as integer division. Otherwise it needs stage 2. |  |
| `--style` `<style>` | compact: each operation calls a runtime routine. inline: simple integer expressions appear as direct 6502 instructions (longer in the source, shorter in the runtime). Values: `compact`, `inline`. | `compact` |
| `--runtime` `<mode>` | include: the runtime comes from data/sys via #include. embed: it is copied into the result file, which can then be assembled without an include folder. Values: `include`, `embed`. | `include` |
| `--no-track-line` | Do not keep a line number at run time: smaller, but error messages have no line. |  |
| `--no-rem` | Do not take lines that consist only of REM. |  |
| `-o` `<file.asm>` | Output file with the assembler source. | source name with .asm |
| `--map` `<file.json>` | Line map: BASIC line, source line and label in the assembler. | source name with .b2a.json |
| `--check` | Only check and report the stage and number of lines. No files are written. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# simple conversion
vcc basic2asm examples/c64/basic_native/sterne.bas -o sterne.asm
```

```bash
# convert for the Atari
vcc basic2asm examples/atari/basic_native/farben.bas --target atari8 -o farben.asm
```

```bash
# Turbo BASIC XL with a stage limit
vcc basic2asm examples/atari/turbo_basic/balken.tur --target atari8 --turbo --stage 2 -o balken.asm
```

```bash
# check only
vcc basic2asm examples/c64/basic_native/sterne.bas --check
```

> **Note:** Commands the converter does not translate (OPEN, LOAD, LIST, NEW ...) are reported (E311), not silently replaced. On the Atari, you always get the note I150 about numbers.

> **Note:** You can print the syntax tree with vcc basic ast.

## `vcc build`

Build a project from its .vcprj

Builds all sources of the project file in build order (assembler and BASIC, including conversion of BASIC to assembler and of media files). If the project file describes a disk, the command creates it afterwards. The results are in the build/ folder of the project.

Turbo BASIC XL projects (dialect turbo_basic_xl, Atari) with a disk in the project (section turbo, see vcc turbo provide) get build/<name>.atr: a copy of the disk with the translated program as AUTORUN.BAS. If the disk is missing, it stays a note (exit code 0).

```
vcc build [project] [options]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `project` | Project folder (the first .vcprj in it) or project file. Without it, the current folder is used. (optional) |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--main` | Builds only the start program (main in the project file). The disk is then not created. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database (data). Replaces VC_DATA and the automatic search. |  |
| `--strict` | Turbo BASIC XL: a missing user disk (section turbo of the project file) is an error (exit code 1) instead of a note. |  |
| `--license-report` | Prints the licenses of all assembled sources (file, license, author, location) and writes them to build/LICENSES.txt. |  |
| `--json` | With --license-report: the report as JSON on standard output (the OK/ERROR lines then go to the error output). |  |
| `--deny-license` `<list>` | The build fails (code L002) if an assembled source is under one of these SPDX licenses, e.g. GPL-3.0-only,GPL-3.0-or-later (a trailing * is a wildcard, e.g. GPL-*). To make it permanent, use "licenses": {"deny": [...]} in the project file. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Build the project in the current folder
vcc build
```

```bash
# Build a project folder
vcc build examples/c64/cart_demo
```

```bash
# List the licenses of the sources
vcc build examples/atari/music_demo --license-report
```

```bash
# start program only
vcc build examples/mega65/prallball/prallball.vcprj --main
```

> **Note:** Each source gets a line OK or ERROR, and the start program is marked. Messages go to the error output.

> **Note:** Warnings about the project file (e.g. missing files from assets) come first. A project without sources is an error.

> **Note:** License note: If a program contains source under a copyleft license (GPL, LGPL, AGPL), a note (L001) appears on the error output. This is not an error. The line SPDX-License-Identifier at the top of the files is read. Files without it stay neutral. In the project file, "licenses": {"allow": [...]} allows a license (no note), and "deny" blocks it.

Exit codes: `0` = everything built · `1` = a source or the disk failed, or no project file found · `2` = wrong usage

## `vcc debuglog`

Analyze the debug log of the IDE

Summarizes the log file that VintageCoder writes when the debug log is turned on (Settings > General or the environment variable VC_DEBUG_LOG). The file consists of JSON lines (ts, seq, kind, msg). The first line contains the version and installation. The output shows the program, the number and kind of entries, crashes, errors and warnings, and the last events before the end.

Without a file, the default file logs/vintagecoder.log in the configuration folder is used. The command only reads and sends nothing.

```
vcc debuglog [file.log] [options]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file.log` | Log file. The default is the file in the configuration folder (or VC_DEBUG_LOG, if it is a path). (optional) |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Print the summary as machine-readable JSON. |  |
| `--tail` `<n>` | Number of last events to show. | 20 |
| `--path` | Print only the path of the default file. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Summarize the default log
vcc debuglog
```

```bash
# Analyze a file from a feedback report, machine-readable
vcc debuglog error.log --json
```

```bash
# Show the path of the default file
vcc debuglog --path
```

> **Note:** Lines that are not a valid entry (for example one cut off by a crash) are counted and skipped.

> **Note:** When the file is rotated (5 MB), the previous file stays with the extension .log.1.

## `vcc dis`

Disassemble a machine program

Prints the disassembly on standard output: address, bytes and instruction per line. Undocumented instructions have the addition "undocumented".

For .prg, the start address is in the file header. Atari XEX files (extension .xex or .com, or header $FFFF) are printed segment by segment with their addresses. For other files, address 0 is used if --start is missing.

```
vcc dis <file> [options]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file` | Program file (.prg, .xex, .bin). |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--start` `<address>` | Start address of the image. The file is then read as raw bytes: for .prg the header counts too, and for XEX the segment split is skipped. | load address for .prg; segment addresses for XEX; otherwise 0 |
| `--cpu` `<cpu>` | CPU instruction set. Values: `45gs02`, `6510`, `7501`, `8502`, `nmos6502`, `sally`. | `6510` |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database (data). Replaces VC_DATA and the automatic search. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Disassemble a C64 program
vcc dis border.prg
```

```bash
# MEGA65 program with 45GS02
vcc dis prallball.prg --cpu 45gs02
```

```bash
# raw image from an address
vcc dis kernal.bin --start $e000
```

> **Note:** Addresses are numbers like 49152, $c000, 0xc000 or %1100. An invalid number for --start is ignored.

> **Note:** The detection of .prg is case-sensitive for the extension.

## `vcc disk`

Create and list disk images and extract files from them

Works with the formats D64 (1541), D71 (1571), D81 (1581) and ATR (Atari, DOS 2). When you create an image, the subcommand sets its type. When you list or extract, the file extension sets it.

With `--add`, the first colon separates the file from the disk name. A path with a drive letter (C:\...) therefore cannot be combined with a name. Use relative paths in that case.

### Form `d64`

Create a D64 image (1541) with programs

```
vcc disk d64 -o <out.d64> [--name <name>] [--id <id>] [--add <file[:NAME]>]...
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-o` `<file>` | Output file of the image. Required. |  |
| `--name` `<name>` | Disk name in the directory header. | `VINTAGECODER` |
| `--id` `<id>` | Disk ID in the directory header. | `VC` |
| `--add` `<file[:NAME]>` | Write a program file (PRG) to the disk, optionally under a different name. Can be repeated. | File name without extension, in uppercase |
| `--keep` | Accepted and ignored. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database. Otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Disk with one program
vcc disk d64 -o game.d64 --name GAME --id 01 --add jumprun.prg:JUMPRUN
```

> **Note:** The output shows the size and the free blocks.

### Form `d71`

Create a D71 image (1571) with programs

```
vcc disk d71 -o <out.d71> [--name <name>] [--id <id>] [--add <file[:NAME]>]...
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-o` `<file>` | Output file of the image. Required. |  |
| `--name` `<name>` | Disk name in the directory header. | `VINTAGECODER` |
| `--id` `<id>` | Disk ID in the directory header. | `VC` |
| `--add` `<file[:NAME]>` | Write a program file (PRG) to the disk, optionally under a different name. Can be repeated. | File name without extension, in uppercase |
| `--keep` | Accepted and ignored. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database. Otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# D71 with one program
vcc disk d71 -o game.d71 --add jumprun.prg
```

### Form `d81`

Create a D81 image (1581) with programs

```
vcc disk d81 -o <out.d81> [--name <name>] [--id <id>] [--add <file[:NAME]>]...
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-o` `<file>` | Output file of the image. Required. |  |
| `--name` `<name>` | Disk name in the directory header. | `VINTAGECODER` |
| `--id` `<id>` | Disk ID in the directory header. | `VC` |
| `--add` `<file[:NAME]>` | Write a program file (PRG) to the disk, optionally under a different name. Can be repeated. | File name without extension, in uppercase |
| `--keep` | Accepted and ignored. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database. Otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# D81 for MEGA65 or C128
vcc disk d81 -o game.d81 --name GAME --add jumprun.prg
```

### Form `atr`

Create an ATR image (Atari DOS 2) with files

```
vcc disk atr -o <out.atr> [--add <file[:NAME.EXT]>]...
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-o` `<file>` | Output file of the image. Required. |  |
| `--add` `<file[:NAME.EXT]>` | Write a file to the DOS 2 file system, optionally under a different name. Can be repeated. | File name in uppercase, with extension |
| `--name` `<name>` | Accepted, but has no effect on ATR images. | `VINTAGECODER` |
| `--id` `<id>` | Accepted, but has no effect on ATR images. | `VC` |
| `--keep` | Accepted and ignored. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database. Otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# ATR with one file as AUTORUN.SYS
vcc disk atr -o game.atr --add jumprun.xex:AUTORUN.SYS
```

> **Note:** The image is 90 KB (720 sectors of 128 bytes). The form `atr-boot` creates a bootable disk without a file system.

### Form `atr-boot`

Create a bootable ATR disk from an XEX program

```
vcc disk atr -o <out.atr> --boot <prog.xex>
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-o` `<file>` | Output file of the image. Required. |  |
| `--boot` `<prog.xex>` | XEX program that the disk loads at power-on (boot loader from the hardware database). Required. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database. It provides the boot loader. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Bootable disk
vcc disk atr -o jumprun.atr --boot jumprun.xex
```

> **Note:** `--boot` cannot be combined with `--add`: the boot disk has no file system. `vcc disk list` reports this.

> **Note:** A file without an XEX signature ($FFFF at the start) causes an error.

### Form `atr-edit`

Change an existing ATR image (replace, delete and add files)

```
vcc disk atr -o <out.atr> --base <in.atr> [--put <file[:NAME.EXT]>]... [--delete <NAME.EXT>]... [--add <file[:NAME.EXT]>]... [--force]
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-o` `<file>` | Output file of the image (not the base image). Required. |  |
| `--base` `<in.atr>` | Base image (ATR, DOS 2); it stays unchanged, the result goes to the output file. Required. |  |
| `--put` `<file[:NAME.EXT]>` | Add a file or replace it, optionally under a different name. Can be repeated. |  |
| `--delete` `<NAME.EXT>` | Delete a file from the disk (its sectors become free). Can be repeated. |  |
| `--add` `<file[:NAME.EXT]>` | Add a file; if the name already exists, that is an error. Can be repeated. |  |
| `--force` | Write-protected files may be deleted with --delete. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Accepted and ignored. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Reduce the base image
vcc disk atr -o new.atr --base turbo.atr --delete COMPILER.COM --delete RUNTIME.COM --force
```

> **Note:** Write-protected files (`*` in vcc disk list) can only be deleted with --force and --put never overwrites them. The image is checked afterwards; on errors no output file is written.

> **Note:** The output shows the size and the free sectors. For Turbo BASIC XL projects see vcc turbo.

### Form `list`

Show and check the directory of an image

```
vcc disk list <image.d64|d71|d81|atr>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `image` | Disk image. The extension (d64, d71, d81, atr) sets the format. |

Examples:

```bash
# Show the directory
vcc disk list game.d64
```

```bash
# Show an Atari disk
vcc disk list game.atr
```

> **Note:** Commodore: block count, name, file type and free blocks. Atari: name, sectors, start sector, `*` for protected files, and free sectors.

> **Note:** The check (BAM or VTOC, directory, file chains) reports differences as "Problem:" on stderr.

Exit codes: `0` = no errors · `1` = file not readable or problem found in the image · `2` = wrong usage

### Form `extract`

Extract a file from an image

```
vcc disk extract <image.d64|d71|d81|atr> <NAME> [-o <file>]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `image` | Disk image. The extension sets the format. |
| `NAME` | File name on the disk. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-o` `<file>` | Target file. | Commodore: NAME in lowercase with extension .prg; Atari: NAME in lowercase |

Examples:

```bash
# Extract a program from a D64
vcc disk extract game.d64 JUMPRUN -o jumprun.prg
```

```bash
# Extract a file from an ATR
vcc disk extract game.atr AUTORUN.SYS -o autorun.sys
```

## `vcc emulator`

Show, find and install emulators portably

Shows the emulators that VintageCoder uses (VICE, atari800, Altirra, Xemu, Fujisan), with homepage, license and role. `install` downloads a fixed version from the project's site, only when you call it explicitly. It checks the SHA-256 sum and unpacks it below VintageCoder (`emulators/<Emulator>/<Version>` in the configuration folder). Nothing is shipped and nothing is downloaded without this call.

### Form `list`

show the emulators of the catalog with homepage and role

```
vcc emulator list
```

Examples:

```bash
# list all emulators
vcc emulator list
```

### Form `status`

show what is found (all sources) and what can be installed

```
vcc emulator status [emulator]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `emulator` | ID (vice, atari800, altirra, xemu, fujisan) or variant (x64sc, x128 ...). Without it, all. (optional) |

Examples:

```bash
# check all emulators
vcc emulator status
```

```bash
# check one emulator
vcc emulator status atari800
```

> **Note:** The automatic order is: path from the settings, otherwise what PATH and the usual program folders offer, and last the newest portably installed version.

### Form `install`

download a fixed version, check it and install it portably

```
vcc emulator install <emulator[@version]> [options]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `emulator[@version]` | ID (vice, atari800, altirra, xemu, fujisan) or variant (x64sc, x128 ...), optionally with a version (vice@3.9). Without a version, the default (the newest) is used. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Only shows the package, address, checksum and target folder, without downloading anything. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# show what would be downloaded
vcc emulator install atari800 --dry-run
```

```bash
# download and install Fujisan
vcc emulator install fujisan
```

```bash
# install an older version alongside
vcc emulator install vice@3.9
```

> **Note:** Uses `curl` and `tar` of the system (Windows 10/11 and Linux include them). Where there is no portable package (e.g. macOS, VICE on Linux), the command names the download page.

> **Note:** If the version is already installed, nothing happens. If the checksum does not match, the file is deleted and nothing is unpacked.

> **Note:** In the automatic search, portably installed programs come after PATH and the usual program folders. A path in the settings and a version chosen with `@version` take priority.

> **Note:** Several versions of an emulator can exist side by side. `vcc emulator status` shows all sources found (portable and system) and the versions that can be downloaded. `vcc test --backend vice@3.9` uses a specific one.

Exit codes: `0` = installed or already present · `1` = error (network, checksum, unpacking, no package) · `2` = unknown emulator

## `vcc feedback`

Prepare feedback by email with details about the installation

Puts together the subject and text of a mail to vintagecoder@drueeke.de: version, commit, operating system, architecture, kind and folder of the installation, data folder, configuration folder, release choice and, with --target, the target system. Paths in your home folder appear as ~. Project names are not included.

Without --open, the command only prints what the mail would contain. With --open, the operating system opens the default mail program with the subject and text filled in. Nothing is sent until you click Send there. You add the error description, screenshots and attachments there yourself. There is no network access and no telemetry.

```
vcc feedback [optionen]
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--open` | Open the mail in the default mail program (macOS open, Windows rundll32, Linux xdg-open). | print only |
| `--json` | Print everything as machine-readable JSON (subject, text, link, single details). |  |
| `--target` `<system>` | Include the target system of the project in the details, e.g. c64. | no target system |

Examples:

```bash
# see what the mail would contain
vcc feedback
```

```bash
# open the mail in the mail program
vcc feedback --open
```

```bash
# as JSON, with target system
vcc feedback --json --target c64
```

> **Note:** The mailto link is limited to about 1900 characters (Windows handles about 2000). If the mail does not fit, the optional details are left out and the text says which. The --json output contains the full text as body_full.

> **Note:** With --open and no mail program, the command ends with error code 1. The subject and text are still in the output.

## `vcc import`

Bring programs and files from disks, or single files, into the project

Takes files from disk images (D64, D71, D81, ATR), or single PRG, XEX and BASIC files, into a project folder. Without a name and without `--all`, the command only shows the directory.

### Form `verzeichnis`

Show the directory of an image

```
vcc import <image.d64|d71|d81|atr> [--data-dir <path>]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `image` | Disk image (extension d64, d71, d81 or atr). |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database. Otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Show the directory
vcc import game.d64
```

> **Note:** For each file, shows the name, type, size and load address. For detected BASIC programs, it also shows the dialect and line count (only with the hardware database). Nothing is written.

### Form `image`

Import files from an image into the project

```
vcc import <image.d64|d71|d81|atr> (<NAME>... | --all) [--into <project-folder>] [--dir <folder>] [--asm [--cpu <id>]] [--raw] [--no-basic]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `image` | Disk image (extension d64, d71, d81 or atr). |
| `NAME` | File name on the disk (case does not matter). Use --all instead. (optional) Can be repeated. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` | Imports all files of the image. |  |
| `--into` `<project-folder>` | Project folder that the files are imported into. | `.` |
| `--dir` `<folder>` | Subfolder in the project that the files are written to. | `import` |
| `--asm` | Also creates a disassembled source file (.asm) for machine programs. This is purely mechanical: data appears as instructions. |  |
| `--cpu` `<id>` | Processor for disassembling with --asm (name of a file in data/cpus). | 6510, or sally for Atari programs |
| `--raw` | Also keeps the unchanged original file when a BASIC program is imported as source text. |  |
| `--no-basic` | Does not detect BASIC and copies the files unchanged. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database. Otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Import one file
vcc import game.d64 JUMPRUN --into myproject
```

```bash
# All files with source text
vcc import game.atr --all --asm --dir sources
```

> **Note:** BASIC programs are imported as readable .bas source text. Existing files in the target folder are kept (the new file name gets a suffix _2, _3 ...).

> **Note:** The exit code is 1 if a file could not be imported or a name is not on the disk.

### Form `datei`

Import a single program into the project

```
vcc import <file.prg|file.xex|file.bas> [--into <project-folder>] [--dir <folder>] [--asm [--cpu <id>]] [--raw] [--no-basic]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file` | PRG, XEX or BASIC file (not a disk image). |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--into` `<project-folder>` | Project folder that the files are imported into. | `.` |
| `--dir` `<folder>` | Subfolder in the project that the files are written to. | `import` |
| `--asm` | Also creates a disassembled source file (.asm) for machine programs. This is purely mechanical: data appears as instructions. |  |
| `--cpu` `<id>` | Processor for disassembling with --asm (name of a file in data/cpus). | 6510, or sally for Atari programs |
| `--raw` | Also keeps the unchanged original file when a BASIC program is imported as source text. |  |
| `--no-basic` | Does not detect BASIC and copies the files unchanged. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database. Otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Atari program with source text
vcc import jumprun.xex --asm --into myproject
```

```bash
# Import a BASIC program
vcc import stars.prg --into myproject
```

> **Note:** A file counts as an Atari program if it has an XEX signature or is a tokenized Atari BASIC file (.bas). It also counts as a program if it has the extension .prg.

## `vcc inc`

Print an include file with hardware constants

Creates an include file from the hardware database (data/chips) with the registers of the chips of the target system as .const lines. Without -o, the text goes to standard output.

```
vcc inc --target <system> [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--target` `<system>` | Target system whose chips are printed. Values: `atari8`, `c128`, `c64`, `mega65`, `pet`, `plus4`, `vic20`. Required. |  |
| `-o` `<file.inc>` | Output file. Without the option, the text appears on the screen. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database (data). Replaces VC_DATA and the automatic search. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Print C64 constants
vcc inc --target c64
```

```bash
# Atari constants to a file
vcc inc --target atari8 -o atari.inc
```

## `vcc media`

Work with sprites, character sets, songs and other media files

Also as: `vcc asset`.

Works with the media files of a project (graphics/NAME.vcsprite, .vcpmg, .vcchar, .vcscreen, .vctiles, .vcpal; music/NAME.vcsong, .vcplay). The project folder is the current folder.

### Form `new`

create a new media file from a profile

```
vcc media new <name> --profile <id> [--dir <dir>] [--blank]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | Name of the file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--profile` `<id>` | Profile that sets the kind and layout (sprite, character set, screen, tiles, song, palette ...). Required. |  |
| `--dir` `<dir>` | Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder). | default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics |
| `--blank` | Creates a character set that is empty, instead of one with a reference to the default character set of the system. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Create a character set
vcc media new font --profile c64.char.hires
```

```bash
# Empty character set in a subfolder
vcc media new spiel --profile c64.char.hires --blank --dir graphics/fonts
```

```bash
# Multicolor sprite
vcc media new hero --profile c64.sprite.multicolor
```

> **Note:** A new character set starts with a reference to the default character set of the system in your ROM; --blank creates it empty.

> **Note:** If the folder has a .vcprj, the target system of the profile must match the systems of the project.

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

> **Note:** Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

### Form `import-sprite`

import sprites from SPD, raw data or another sprite asset

```
vcc media import-sprite <source> --name <name> [--profile <id>] [--offset <n>] [--count <n>] [--mode hires|multicolor] [--frame <n>] [--dir <dir>]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `source` | SPD file (.spd), sprite file (.vcsprite, .vcpmg) or raw data in 64-byte blocks (.bin, .prg ...). |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--name` `<name>` | Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed. Required. |  |
| `--profile` `<id>` | Target profile (a sprite or PMG profile). | `c64.sprite.hires` |
| `--dir` `<dir>` | Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder). | default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics |
| `--offset` `<n>` | Raw data: byte offset of the first sprite (decimal, $hex, 0xhex or %binary). For .prg, the two bytes of the load address are added. | `0` |
| `--count` `<n>` | Raw data: number of sprites; 0 means all complete blocks from the offset (at most 256). | `0` |
| `--mode` `<mode>` | Raw data: mode of the sprites; multicolor can be shortened to mc. Values: `hires`, `multicolor`, `mc`. | mode of the target profile |
| `--frame` `<n>` | When switching to Atari PMG: number of the source sprite (0-based) that is imported. | `0` |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Import an SPD file
vcc media import-sprite figuren.spd --name figuren
```

```bash
# Raw data, five multicolor sprites
vcc media import-sprite sprites.bin --name raw --offset 0 --count 5 --mode multicolor
```

```bash
# C64 sprite as Atari PMG
vcc media import-sprite graphics/hero.vcsprite --name hero_pmg --profile atari.pmg.single --frame 0
```

> **Note:** Sprite import into profiles of systems other than C64 is supported only for PMG (Atari). The output shows the path and the number of frames; notes go to stderr.

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

> **Note:** Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

### Form `import-song`

import a song from GoatTracker, SID or a song file

```
vcc media import-song <source> --name <name> [--profile <id>] [--song <n>] [--seconds <n>] [--dir <dir>]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `source` | GoatTracker song (.sng), SID file (.sid) or song file (.vcsong) of a project. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--name` `<name>` | Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed. Required. |  |
| `--profile` `<id>` | Target profile of the song (different chip: conversion). | `c64.sid.song` |
| `--dir` `<dir>` | Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder). | default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics |
| `--song` `<n>` | SID file: number of the subtune (from 1); 0 takes the start song of the file. | `0` |
| `--seconds` `<n>` | SID file: seconds recorded from the play routine. | `30` |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# GoatTracker song
vcc media import-song lied.sng --name lied
```

```bash
# Record a SID (20 seconds, subtune 2)
vcc media import-song musik.sid --name musik --song 2 --seconds 20
```

```bash
# Import a song for the MEGA65
vcc media import-song music/tune.vcsong --name tune4 --profile mega65.sid4.song
```

> **Note:** With the same chip, the song is imported (voices are padded if the target has more); otherwise it is converted. Notes go to stderr.

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

> **Note:** Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

### Form `convert`

convert a song to the profile of a different chip

```
vcc media convert <song.vcsong> --profile <id> --name <name> [--dir <dir>]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `song.vcsong` | Song file in the project. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--profile` `<id>` | Target profile with a different chip (e.g. atari.pokey.song). Required. |  |
| `--name` `<name>` | Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed. Required. |  |
| `--dir` `<dir>` | Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder). | default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# C64 song for POKEY
vcc media convert music/tune.vcsong --profile atari.pokey.song --name tune_pokey
```

> **Note:** If source and target have the same chip, the command stops; use `import-song` for that. Notes about the conversion (shortened envelopes, shifted octaves) go to stderr.

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

> **Note:** Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

### Form `import-rmt`

import an RMT module as a POKEY song

```
vcc media import-rmt <module.rmt> --name <name> [--dir <dir>]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `module.rmt` | RMT module (Raster Music Tracker) in the project. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--name` `<name>` | Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed. Required. |  |
| `--dir` `<dir>` | Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder). | default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Import an RMT module
vcc media import-rmt tune_pokey.rmt --name pokey
```

> **Note:** The result always has the profile atari.pokey.song. Notes go to stderr.

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

### Form `import-rom`

import a character set from a ROM image

```
vcc media import-rom <rom> --profile <id> --name <name> [--offset <n>] [--dir <dir>]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rom` | ROM image (any path). |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--profile` `<id>` | Character set profile of the target. Required. |  |
| `--name` `<name>` | Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed. Required. |  |
| `--offset` `<n>` | Byte offset of the character set in the image (decimal, $hex, 0xhex or %binary). | `0` |
| `--dir` `<dir>` | Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder). | default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Second C64 character set from chargen.bin
vcc media import-rom chargen.bin --profile c64.char.hires --offset 0x800 --name klein
```

> **Note:** If --profile or --name is missing, the command shows on stderr what it detected (size, checksum) and lists matching profiles and offsets (exit code 2).

> **Note:** ROM images of original devices are protected by copyright; the copy contains the original characters. For a project that will be published, use `std-charset` (reference) instead.

> **Note:** The character set is saved as .vcchar in the target folder (default graphics).

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

> **Note:** Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

Exit codes: `0` = no error · `1` = error · `2` = wrong usage (also: --profile or --name is missing)

### Form `std-charset-liste`

list sources of default character sets with their status

```
vcc media std-charset
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Show sources
vcc media std-charset
```

> **Note:** One line each, separated by tabs: reference, profile, system, ROM status, description.

### Form `std-charset`

add a default character set to the project as a reference or copy

```
vcc media std-charset <ref> [--profile <id>] [--copy] [--dir <dir>]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ref` | ROM reference of the form rom:system/role#set, e.g. rom:c64/chargen#upper. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--profile` `<id>` | Character set profile. | the profile that the list gives for the reference |
| `--copy` | Embeds the characters in the file (format 1) and writes to graphics/standard/, instead of saving only a reference. |  |
| `--dir` `<dir>` | Target folder in the project; without --copy. | `graphics` |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Reference to the C64 character set
vcc media std-charset rom:c64/chargen#upper --profile c64.char.hires
```

```bash
# Embed the characters
vcc media std-charset rom:c64/chargen#upper --profile c64.char.hires --copy
```

> **Note:** The file is named <system>_<set>.vcchar. Without --copy, the file contains only the reference; the original characters stay in the user's ROM. Embedded copies are not meant to be checked in or passed on.

> **Note:** If the ROM is missing, the file is still created; a note goes to stderr.

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

> **Note:** Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

### Form `import-sheet`

import a character set from a PNG grid

```
vcc media import-sheet <grid.png> --profile <id> --name <name> [--invert] [--dir <dir>]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `grid.png` | PNG with 16 characters per row in reading order (enlargement by a whole number is allowed). |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--profile` `<id>` | Character set profile with 1 bit per pixel or MEGA65 full color. Required. |  |
| `--name` `<name>` | Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed. Required. |  |
| `--invert` | Dark pixels count as set instead of light ones. |  |
| `--dir` `<dir>` | Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder). | default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Grid as character set
vcc media import-sheet font.png --profile c64.char.hires --name font
```

```bash
# Dark characters on a light background
vcc media import-sheet font.png --profile c64.char.hires --name font2 --invert
```

> **Note:** The image must fit 16 columns and be a whole multiple of the character size (128 x 128 pixels for 256 characters of 8 x 8). Transparent pixels count as not set.

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

> **Note:** Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

### Form `export-sheet`

write a character set as a PNG grid

```
vcc media export-sheet <charset.vcchar> <output.png>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `charset.vcchar` | Character set in the project. |
| `output.png` | Target file. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Character set as image
vcc media export-sheet graphics/font.vcchar font.png
```

> **Note:** The grid has 16 characters per row, white on black, 1:1. Only character sets with 1 bit per pixel and MEGA65 full color.

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

### Form `import`

read a PNG image into a frame of a sprite, PMG or character set

```
vcc media import <file> <image.png> [--frame <n>] [--system <pal|ntsc>] [--keep-colors]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file` | Media file in the project (.vcsprite, .vcpmg or .vcchar) with embedded frames. |
| `image.png` | PNG; scaled to the frame size, pixels below 50 % opacity are transparent. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--frame` `<n>` | Number of the frame that is overwritten (0-based). | `0` |
| `--system` `<standard>` | Video standard of the palette, pal or ntsc; only affects the Atari. | `pal` |
| `--keep-colors` | Keeps the colors of the file and rounds the image colors to them; otherwise the colors of the file are taken from the image. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Image into sprite frame 0
vcc media import graphics/hero.vcsprite hero.png
```

```bash
# With fixed colors, frame 2
vcc media import graphics/hero.vcsprite hero.png --frame 2 --keep-colors
```

> **Note:** Only for profiles with at most 16 colors. If the image does not fit the available colors, the command reports a color conflict and rounds to the nearest colors; the replaced colors are shown in the output.

> **Note:** The file is changed in place.

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

### Form `export`

write a media file as assembler, binary data or BASIC DATA

```
vcc media export <file> [--format <asm|inc|bin|prg|data|sbas|rmt|bas>] [--label <name>] [--address <address>]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file` | Media file in the project (.vcsprite, .vcpmg, .vcchar, .vcscreen, .vctiles, .vcpal, .vcsong, .vcplay). |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--format` `<format>` | Output format: asm (.byte data and .const), inc (only .const for length and, with --address, address), bin, prg (with load address, needs --address), data (BASIC DATA with @label), sbas (DATA for structured BASIC). POKEY songs: asm or rmt; PLAY songs: bas or data. Values: `asm`, `inc`, `bin`, `prg`, `data`, `sbas`, `rmt`, `bas`. | `asm` |
| `--label` `<name>` | Label of the data in the source code; parts get a suffix. | name of the file, with - replaced by _ |
| `--address` `<address>` | Load address for prg, address for inc, and for rmt the load address of the module ($hex, 0xhex or decimal). | for rmt: $4000 |
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Character set as assembler
vcc media export graphics/font.vcchar --format asm
```

```bash
# Sprite as PRG at $2000
vcc media export graphics/hero.vcsprite --format prg --address 0x2000
```

```bash
# Song as BASIC DATA
vcc media export music/tune.vcsong --format data --label tune
```

```bash
# POKEY song as RMT module
vcc media export music/tune_pokey.vcsong --format rmt --address 0x4000
```

> **Note:** The files are created in build/export/; the command prints the path and size of each file. If the output has several parts (screens: chars/attrs, tiles: tiles/map/colors), each part gets its own file or section.

> **Note:** Media files can also be included directly with #include; this export is not needed for that.

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

### Form `migrate-tiles`

convert old tile maps to a tile set and a screen bank

```
vcc media migrate-tiles
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` `<path>` | Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Convert the project
vcc media migrate-tiles
```

> **Note:** Looks in the current project folder for old tile maps (*.vctiles of kind tilemap). Files of a folder with the same tile set result in one tile set and one screen bank. The old files are removed.

> **Note:** The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

## `vcc migrate`

Convert a project from the old file scheme to the new one

Renames files in the old scheme (*.asset.json) to <name>.vc<kind>, moves assets/ to graphics/ or music/, and build/assets/ to build/export/. References in sources, includes and assets are updated too. Every rename is printed. build/export/ is created again at the next build.

### Basic form

Convert a project from the old file scheme to the new one

```
vcc migrate [project-folder]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `project-folder` | Root of the project. The default is the working folder. (optional) |

Examples:

```bash
# Convert the project in the working folder
vcc migrate
```

```bash
# convert a specific project
vcc migrate examples/c64/tests_demo
```

> **Note:** If there is nothing to convert, the output is: nothing to convert.

> **Note:** The command has no options. The first argument is taken as the folder.

### Form `includes`

Convert old include paths build/export/… to the media file

```
vcc migrate includes [projectfolder] [--apply]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `projectfolder` | Project root; default is the working folder. (optional) |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--apply` | Actually write the conversion; without this option it only shows what would change. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Show what would change
vcc migrate includes
```

```bash
# Write the conversion
vcc migrate includes examples/c64/jumprun --apply
```

> **Note:** Turns .include "build/export/hero.asm" into .include "graphics/hero.vcsprite" (BASIC: #include). A line with hero.anim.asm directly after it is removed: including the media file delivers data and tables together.

> **Note:** If a name matches no media file or several in the project, the line stays unchanged and is reported.

## `vcc new`

Create a new project from a template

Creates the folder (if needed) and writes the project file <name>.vcprj and the sources of the template, per target system under src/<system>/. The folder must not contain a .vcprj yet.

With --structure, the folders and layout of a project structure are added. vcc new --list shows templates, variants and project structures with the possible target systems.

```
vcc new <folder> [options]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `folder` | Project folder. Its name is the project name if --name is missing. Not needed with --list. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--target` `<system[,system...]>` | Target systems, separated by commas. Each gets its own sources under src/<system>/. The template must support the system. | `c64` |
| `--template` `<template>` | File template: assembler program, BASIC or only the project file with src/. Values: `asm-hello`, `basic-hello`, `empty`. | `asm-hello` |
| `--variant` `<variant>` | Variant of the template. cartridge creates an 8 KB cartridge instead of a program (asm-hello only; c64, atari8, vic20). Values: `cartridge`. | none |
| `--structure` `<structure>` | Project structure: creates folders and enters the layout in the project file. Your own templates from structures.json are also possible. The earlier German names (einfach, gross, mehrsystem, bibliothek, spiel) are still accepted. Values: `simple`, `standard`, `large`, `multisystem`, `library`, `game`. | none |
| `--charset` `<choice>` | Character set of the project: auto = your ROM as a reference, otherwise the own default set as a copy; own = always the own default set (can be passed on, with HERKUNFT.txt); none = none. Values: `auto`, `own`, `none`. | `auto` |
| `--name` `<name>` | Project name (letters, digits, _ and -, at most 48 characters). Sets the name of the .vcprj. | name of the folder |
| `--list` | List project structures, templates and variants with their target systems. Creates nothing. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database (data). | VC_DATA, otherwise next to the program or in the working folder |

Examples:

```bash
# simple C64 project
vcc new game --target c64
```

```bash
# one project for several targets
vcc new multi --target c64,atari8
```

```bash
# BASIC project with a project structure
vcc new demo --target c64,vic20 --template basic-hello --structure multisystem
```

```bash
# cartridge for the VIC-20
vcc new cart --target vic20 --variant cartridge
```

```bash
# list templates and structures
vcc new --list
```

> **Note:** The template empty exists for c64, c128, plus4, vic20, atari8 and mega65. asm-hello also exists for pet, and basic-hello for pet.

> **Note:** Without your own ROM, auto puts the own set VC-Standard (CC0) in graphics/vc-standard/. Systems without an own set (PET) get nothing.

> **Note:** The folders and files that were created are printed.

## `vcc organize`

Rearrange project files according to the project structure

Moves files of the project into the folders given by rules, layout and assets in the project file. Paths in .include/.incbin in the sources and the project file are updated. A backup is made first in .vcbackup/.

These stay where they are: programs of the source groups, start program, disk files, editor files (without a folder for studio in layout), .vctest files (except in a folder with the role tests), the project file, README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG and files already in the target folder. If the target is taken, the file is skipped.

After moving, a check build rebuilds the project and compares the result files with those from before. If they differ, the command ends with exit code 1.

```
vcc organize [project] [options]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `project` | Project folder or .vcprj file. The default is the working folder. (optional) |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Show planned moves and sources to be adjusted. Changes nothing. |  |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Run without asking. Without a terminal, --yes is required, otherwise the command changes nothing. | asks in the terminal |
| `--subdirs` | Also rearrange files in subfolders, not only those in the project folder. | project folder only |
| `--no-rewrite` | Do not adjust paths in .include/.incbin in the sources. | paths are adjusted |
| `--no-check` | Skip the check build before and after moving. | check build runs |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database (data) for the check build. If it is not found, the check build is skipped with a note. | VC_DATA, otherwise next to the program or in the working folder |

Examples:

```bash
# see what would be moved
vcc organize game --dry-run
```

```bash
# run with a prompt
vcc organize game
```

```bash
# without a prompt, including subfolders
vcc organize game --subdirs --yes
```

> **Note:** If the check build differs: copy the files back from .vcbackup/<time>/ and move the files named in moves.txt back. The last five backups are kept.

> **Note:** If there are no files to move, the command reports "Nothing to organize."

Exit codes: `0` = no errors or cancelled · `1` = error, missing confirmation without a terminal, or different check build

## `vcc roms`

Show, check and import ROM files

Manages the ROM images that emulators and checks need. The systems are c64, c128, vic20, plus4, atari8 and mega65. A role is a single ROM of a system (e.g. c64/kernal). You can replace the ROM folder with VC_ROMS.

### Form `list`

show the status per system and role

```
vcc roms list [system] [optionen]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `system` | Show only this system. (optional) |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Print the list as JSON. |  |
| `--foreign` | Also search the ROM folders of other programs. |  |
| `--project` `<folder>` | Project folder to search for ROMs first. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database. | VC_DATA, otherwise next to the program or in the working folder |

Examples:

```bash
# all systems
vcc roms list
```

```bash
# C64 only, as JSON
vcc roms list c64 --json
```

> **Note:** A status is Recognized, Unknown revision, Replacement (free), Missing or Not usable.

### Form `check`

check that the required ROMs are present

```
vcc roms check [system ...] [optionen]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `system` | Systems to check. Without it, all systems. (optional) Can be repeated. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--foreign` | Also search the ROM folders of other programs. |  |
| `--project` `<folder>` | Project folder to search for ROMs first. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database. | VC_DATA, otherwise next to the program or in the working folder |

Examples:

```bash
# Check all systems
vcc roms check
```

```bash
# Check C64 and Atari
vcc roms check c64 atari8
```

> **Note:** Replacement ROMs count as present. If something is missing and matching files are in other programs, the output names vcc roms import --from-others.

Exit codes: `0` = all required ROMs present · `1` = a required ROM is missing · `2` = unknown system

### Form `path`

print the path of the ROM file in use

```
vcc roms path <system/role> [optionen]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `system/role` | System and role, e.g. c64/kernal. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--foreign` | Also search the ROM folders of other programs. |  |
| `--project` `<folder>` | Project folder to search for ROMs first. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database. | VC_DATA, otherwise next to the program or in the working folder |

Examples:

```bash
# Path of the C64 KERNAL
vcc roms path c64/kernal
```

Exit codes: `0` = path printed · `1` = the file is missing or not usable · `2` = argument is not in the form system/role

### Form `where`

show the ROM folder, search locations and portable mode

```
vcc roms where [optionen]
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--foreign` | Also search the ROM folders of other programs. |  |
| `--project` `<folder>` | Project folder to search for ROMs first. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database. | VC_DATA, otherwise next to the program or in the working folder |

Examples:

```bash
# Show the search locations
vcc roms where
```

```bash
# with ROMs of other programs
vcc roms where --foreign
```

> **Note:** Shows the write target, user folder, portable mode, cache and the searched places in the order of the search.

### Form `import`

copy recognized ROMs to the ROM folder

```
vcc roms import <file|folder> ... [optionen]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file|folder` | Files or folders with ROM images. Not needed with --from-others. Can be repeated. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--system` `<system>` | Assigns the files to this system instead of recognizing it. |  |
| `--from-others` | Takes matching ROMs from the folders of other programs instead of from files. |  |
| `--yes` | Really copies. Without --yes, the command only shows a preview. |  |
| `--foreign` | Also search the ROM folders of other programs. |  |
| `--project` `<folder>` | Project folder to search for ROMs first. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database. | VC_DATA, otherwise next to the program or in the working folder |

Examples:

```bash
# Preview for a folder
vcc roms import ~/Downloads/c64roms
```

```bash
# Take ROMs of other programs
vcc roms import --from-others --yes
```

> **Note:** Without --yes, nothing is copied.

Exit codes: `0` = preview printed, or files copied · `1` = copying failed · `2` = no files given

### Form `emit-known`

create entries for data/roms/known.json from real files

```
vcc roms emit-known [optionen]
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--into` `<file.json>` | Writes to this table (read and extended if it exists). Without it, output goes to stdout. |  |
| `--vice` `<folder>` | Takes the ROMs from a VICE data folder. |  |
| `--merge-json` `<file.json>` | Adds entries from a JSON list in the format of known.json. Can be repeated. |  |
| `--file` `<file>` | Starts an entry for this ROM file. The options that follow belong to it. Can be repeated. |  |
| `--as` `<system/role>` | System and role of the entry. Can be repeated. |  |
| `--rev` `<rev>` | Revision of the entry. Can be repeated. |  |
| `--free` | Marks the ROM as free (replacement ROM). Can be repeated. |  |
| `--default` | Marks the revision as the default of the role. Can be repeated. |  |
| `--note` `<text>` | Note for the entry. Can be repeated. |  |
| `--set` `<name:offset:size:profile[:text]>` | Names a range of the ROM (offset, size, profile). Can be repeated. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# From VICE data into a table
vcc roms emit-known --vice /usr/lib/vice --into known.json
```

```bash
# Add one file
vcc roms emit-known --file kernal.bin --as c64/kernal --rev 901227-03 --into known.json
```

> **Note:** Tool for maintaining the database. --as, --rev, --free, --default, --note and --set apply to the --file before them. --as is required for each --file.

Exit codes: `0` = table printed or written · `1` = at least one entry failed · `2` = option without a preceding --file, or unknown option

## `vcc streams`

Receive the video, audio and debug streams of an Ultimate 64

Works with the data streams of an Ultimate 64 on the network. The subcommands start the streams, analyze them and stop them again. They change neither the configuration of the device nor the flash.

### Form `shot`

Save an image of the Ultimate as PNG

```
vcc streams shot --host <host> --out <file.png> [optionen]
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` `<host>` | Address of the Ultimate 64. Required. |  |
| `--out` `<file.png>` | Target file of the image. Required. |  |
| `--password` `<pw>` | Network password. Otherwise the password of the machine with the same address from the settings. |  |
| `--multicast` | Receives the streams via multicast. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Save an image
vcc streams shot --host 192.168.1.64 --out image.png
```

> **Note:** Waits at most 5 seconds for a complete image.

Exit codes: `0` = image saved · `1` = no image received, or error · `2` = unknown option

### Form `listen`

Listen to a song on the real SID of the Ultimate

```
vcc streams listen --host <host> <song.vcsong> [optionen]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `song.vcsong` | Song that is loaded as a player program. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` `<host>` | Address of the Ultimate 64. Required. |  |
| `--password` `<pw>` | Network password. Otherwise the password of the machine with the same address from the settings. |  |
| `--multicast` | Receives the streams via multicast. |  |
| `--secs` `<seconds>` | Playback duration in seconds. Values outside 2 to 120 are limited to that range. | `6` |
| `--wav` `<file.wav>` | Writes the received audio as a WAV file (source rate). |  |
| `--ntsc` | Builds the player program and calculates the rate for NTSC instead of PAL. |  |
| `--keep` | Lets the Ultimate keep running after listening, instead of resetting it. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Listen for six seconds and save as WAV
vcc streams listen --host 192.168.1.64 song.vcsong --wav song.wav
```

> **Note:** Loads the player program onto the Ultimate and resets it. Its running state is lost.

> **Note:** At the end, prints packets, losses and buffer statistics.

Exit codes: `0` = audio received · `1` = error, or no packets received · `2` = unknown option

### Form `probe`

Start the streams, count packets, and print rate and losses

```
vcc streams probe --host <host> [optionen]
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` `<host>` | Address of the Ultimate 64. Required. |  |
| `--password` `<pw>` | Network password. Otherwise the password of the machine with the same address from the settings. |  |
| `--multicast` | Receives the streams via multicast. |  |
| `--video` | Checks the video stream. Without --video, --audio and --debug, video and audio are checked. |  |
| `--audio` | Checks the audio stream. |  |
| `--debug` | Checks the debug stream. It never runs at the same time as the video stream. |  |
