| `--secs` `<seconds>` | Measurement duration in seconds. Values outside 2 to 60 are limited to that range. | `5` |
| `--record` `<folder>` | Writes the received packets of each stream to a .bin file in this folder. |  |
| `--count` `<count>` | Maximum number of packets per stream with --record. | `400` |

Examples:

```bash
# Check video and audio for five seconds
vcc streams probe --host 192.168.1.64
```

```bash
# Check the debug stream
vcc streams probe --host 192.168.1.64 --debug --secs 10
```

> **Note:** --video together with --debug is an error.

> **Note:** For each stream, the output shows the state, packets (per second, Mbit/s), missing and dropped packets, and restarts.

Exit codes: `0` = streams ran without errors · `1` = error in a stream, with --host, or in the recording · `2` = unknown option or subcommand

### Form `trace`

Analyze and summarize the debug stream (6510 Only)

```
vcc streams trace --host <host> [optionen]
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` `<host>` | Address of the Ultimate 64. The debug stream mode on the device must be 6510 Only. Required. |  |
| `--password` `<pw>` | Network password. Otherwise the password of the machine with the same address from the settings. |  |
| `--multicast` | Receives the streams via multicast. |  |
| `--secs` `<seconds>` | Recording duration in seconds. Values outside 1 to 300 are limited to that range. | `5` |
| `--debug` `<file.vcdbg>` | Debug file of the program. It maps instructions to source lines, lists lines that were not reached, and makes symbols usable in --measure. |  |
| `--measure` `<A:B>` | Measures the cycles from address A to address B. Write addresses as $1234, 0x1234, a decimal number, or a symbol from the .vcdbg. Can be repeated. |  |
| `--cpu` `<id>` | CPU description for the instruction table. The 45GS02 is not analyzed. | `6510` |
| `--out` `<file>` | Writes all recorded instructions to this file. |  |
| `--tail` `<count>` | Number of the most recently executed instructions in the output. | `10` |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database. | VC_DATA, otherwise next to the program or in the working folder |

Examples:

```bash
# Record for five seconds
vcc streams trace --host 192.168.1.64
```

```bash
# Measure the cycles between two addresses
vcc streams trace --host 192.168.1.64 --measure $0810:$0820 --secs 3
```

```bash
# With source lines and instruction log
vcc streams trace --host 192.168.1.64 --debug build/prog.vcdbg --out trace.txt
```

> **Note:** Pauses the video stream while the debug stream runs.

> **Note:** The output shows cycles, events (IRQ, NMI), instruction decoding, packet losses, coverage, SID/VIC writes, and the last instructions.

Exit codes: `0` = analysis printed · `1` = error in the stream, unsupported mode, file not readable or writable, invalid address · `2` = unknown option

## `vcc test`

Check tests from *.vctest and run them in an emulator or on hardware

Searches the path for all *.vctest files and first runs their static checks. With --backend, the entries under "tests" also run: in an emulator (vice, atari800, fujisan, xemu) or on real hardware (u64, m65). Without --backend, these tests appear as skipped.

Build first (vcc build): the runner loads the built program. Test files with "mode": "mailbox" check themselves and are read through the mailbox in RAM. Those with "mode": "measure" measure cycles (on the Ultimate 64 only).

Results per test: OK, FAIL, HINT, TIME (timeout), SKIPPED. A summary is printed at the end.

```
vcc test [folder|file.vctest] [options]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `folder|file.vctest` | Folder (searched for *.vctest) or a single test file. The default is the working folder. (optional) |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--backend` `<name>` | Also runs the tests dynamically: vice, atari800 and xemu as emulators, u64 and m65 on real hardware (with address or interface and a safety prompt). | none (static checks only) |
| `--filter` `<text>` | Runs only the dynamic tests that match the text. |  |
| `--prologue` | Forces the prologue in the trap even with VICE, to check the path of the adapters without flag access (trap mode). |  |
| `--poll` | Mailbox tests: reads the mailbox every 100 ms instead of stopping at the endless loop of test_end. |  |
| `--password` `<pw>` | Network password of the Ultimate 64. Otherwise the password of the machine with the same address from the settings. |  |
| `--yes` | Answers the safety prompt before a run on hardware with yes. Without a terminal, --yes is required. |  |
| `--strict` | Turns every hint into an error. |  |
| `--junit` `<file.xml>` | Also writes the result as JUnit XML. |  |
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database. | VC_DATA, otherwise next to the program or in the working folder |

Examples:

```bash
# static checks of a project
vcc test examples/c64/tests_demo
```

```bash
# also run in VICE
vcc test examples/c64/tests_demo --backend vice
```

```bash
# only matching tests in atari800
vcc test examples/atari/prallball --backend atari800 --filter ball
```

```bash
# write the result as JUnit XML
vcc test examples/mega65/prallball --junit ergebnis.xml
```

> **Note:** --backend takes vice, atari800, fujisan, xemu (also with the version of a portably installed build, e.g. vice@3.9), u64:HOST[:PORT] or m65:INTERFACE[@BAUD]. Any other value is an error. u64 and m65 without an address are rejected.

> **Note:** atari800 knows only the target atari8, and Xemu only mega65. VICE runs for c64 (x64sc), c128 (x128), plus4 (xplus4) and vic20 (xvic).

> **Note:** On hardware, reset, loading a program and writing memory lose the running state of the device. Only mailbox tests ("mode": "mailbox") and cycle measurements run there. Trap tests are skipped. Cycle measurements need u64:HOST and the debug stream mode 6510 Only on the device.

> **Note:** If no *.vctest is found, the command ends without error.

Exit codes: `0` = all passed (hints and skipped tests do not count) · `1` = a test failed, a test file is faulty, or a timeout; also path or data folder not found, invalid --backend, hardware prompt declined · `2` = unknown option

## `vcc turbo`

Turbo BASIC XL: provide, check and start the disk

Turbo BASIC XL runs on the Atari from a disk that you must own yourself; VintageCoder does not ship one. The project gets a copy of it (turbo/), building creates build/<name>.atr with the program as AUTORUN.BAS (vcc build), and vcc turbo run starts it in the emulator.

### Form `check`

Check a disk: is it Turbo BASIC XL?

```
vcc turbo check <image.atr> [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `image` | ATR image of the disk (90 KB, Atari DOS 2). |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output as JSON on standard output. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Check a disk
vcc turbo check Turbo_Basic_XL.atr
```

> **Note:** The check only reads bytes (no emulator): file system, AUTORUN.SYS with the TURBO-BASIC XL signature, version, free sectors, directory and SHA-256 against the list of known images. Notes about leftovers (e.g. entries that were never closed) are not errors.

Exit codes: `0` = looks like Turbo BASIC XL, no errors · `1` = not recognized, file system errors or file not readable · `2` = wrong usage

### Form `provide`

Copy the user's disk into the project

```
vcc turbo provide <image.atr> [project] [--reduce] [--yes] [--anyway] [--replace]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `image` | ATR image of your own Turbo BASIC XL disk (only read). |
| `project` | Project folder (with .vcprj). Without it the current folder is used. (optional) |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--reduce` | Reduce the copy to DOS.SYS, DUP.SYS and AUTORUN.SYS (more free space). Asks first; the original stays unchanged. |  |
| `--yes` | Skip the question of --reduce. |  |
| `--anyway` | Use an image even if it does not look like Turbo BASIC XL or has errors (at your own risk). |  |
| `--replace` | Overwrite an existing copy of the same name. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Provide the disk
vcc turbo provide ~/Turbo_Basic_XL.atr meinprojekt
```

```bash
# Provide and reduce
vcc turbo provide ~/Turbo_Basic_XL.atr meinprojekt --reduce
```

> **Note:** Turbo BASIC XL is not part of VintageCoder: you must own the disk yourself. The copy goes to turbo/ under the name of the original; the project file gets the section turbo and the .gitignore the line turbo/*.atr.

Exit codes: `0` = no errors · `1` = image not usable, copy exists or cancelled · `2` = wrong usage

### Form `reduce`

Reduce the copy in the project to the system files

```
vcc turbo reduce [project] [--yes]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `project` | Project folder (with .vcprj). Without it the current folder is used. (optional) |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--yes` | Skip the question. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Make room
vcc turbo reduce
```

> **Note:** Removes everything except DOS.SYS, DUP.SYS and AUTORUN.SYS in the project copy (about 480 instead of 103 sectors are then free; COMPILER.COM, RUNTIME.COM and the sample programs are gone). Your original stays unchanged.

Exit codes: `0` = no errors · `1` = no disk in the project, cannot be reduced or cancelled · `2` = wrong usage

### Form `run`

Build and start in the Atari emulator

```
vcc turbo run [project] [--data-dir <folder>]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `project` | Project folder (with .vcprj). Without it the current folder is used. (optional) |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` `<folder>` | Folder of the hardware database (data); replaces VC_DATA and the automatic search. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# Start a Turbo BASIC XL project
vcc turbo run examples/atari/turbo_basic
```

> **Note:** Builds the main program, writes it as AUTORUN.BAS onto a copy of the disk (build/<name>.atr) and boots it in the default Atari emulator (atari800; Altirra on Windows if chosen) in drive 1 without built-in BASIC. After the program ends (READY), Turbo BASIC XL waits for input. Altirra with a Turbo BASIC XL disk has not been checked yet.

Exit codes: `0` = emulator started · `1` = build error, disk missing or emulator not found · `2` = wrong usage

## `vcc update`

Check whether there is a new version (display only)

Requests the version list (a small file update.json in the release "update-feed" of the public repository, using curl over https), shows whether a newer version exists, and gives the link to the release page. vcc downloads and installs nothing. The call itself is your consent to the one request. The setting "Check for updates" of the user interface has no effect here.

Only the request for the list is sent: address, IP address and the neutral user agent "VintageCoder-update" (without a version number). No ID, no usage data. Other vcc commands never check for updates and do not mention them. If the package has no update check (selection IDE-UPDATE), the command ends with code 2.

```
vcc update [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--check` | Check and show the result (this is also the default without an option). |  |
| `--notes` | Also print the changes since the installed version (Markdown, links and images as plain text). |  |
| `--json` | Print the result as machine-readable JSON. |  |
| `--offline` | Request nothing: show the saved result of the last check. |  |

Examples:

```bash
# check
vcc update
```

```bash
# with the changes
vcc update --check --notes
```

```bash
# in a script (return value 10 = update available)
vcc update --check --json
```

```bash
# without network: the saved result
vcc update --offline
```

> **Note:** The link always points to the fixed address https://github.com/CDrueeke/VintageCoder/releases/tag/v<version>. An address from the version list is never used.

> **Note:** The command writes the check log and the result to the folder updates in the configuration folder (VC_UPDATE_DIR changes the location).

> **Note:** You can change the source with VC_UPDATE_URL (local folder or file, otherwise https only). This never changes the target of the link.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `VC_DATA` | Folder of the hardware database (data); otherwise next to the program or in the working folder. |
| `VC_ROMS` | The user's ROM folder (instead of roms/ in the configuration folder). |
| `VC_XEMU` | Path to the Xemu program (MEGA65 emulator). |
| `VC_XEMU_SD` | Folder with MEGA65.ROM for Xemu. |
| `VC_XEMU_ARGS` | Extra arguments when starting Xemu, separated by spaces. |
| `VC_STRUCTURES` | File with your own project templates (otherwise structures.json in the configuration folder). |
| `VC_UPDATE_URL` | Source of the version list for vcc update (folder, file or https address; otherwise the fixed release update-feed). Never changes the target of the link. |
| `VC_UPDATE_DIR` | Folder for the result and check log of the update check (otherwise updates in the configuration folder). |
| `VC_DEBUG_LOG` | Turn on the debug log: 1 (default file logs/vintagecoder.log in the configuration folder) or a file path; 0 turns it off. Applies to vintagecoder and vcc. |
| `VC_WIN` | Window size of the IDE, e.g. 1400x860 (vintagecoder only). |
| `COLUMNS` | Width for line wrapping of the help (default: 100). |
| `NO_COLOR` | No colors in the help output. |

## Exit codes

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | no errors |
| `1` | error (in the source, in a check or during execution) |
| `2` | wrong usage (unknown command or unknown option) |
